note: Machine register of known limitations carried by the M0-D closeout. Every entry stays OPEN until a separate, Receipt-backed Owner Decision or a reviewed successor change closes it. The register grants no authorization (contract section 11). Entries are never deleted; an entry fixed in the repository keeps its original text and status OPEN and gains a resolution block (state FIXED_IN_REPO_PENDING_PROD_APPLY) and a history entry until it is closed as above; a closed entry keeps its text, gains status CLOSED, the closing Decision in resolution.closure and a history entry. review_dispositions records how each B09 finding was handled; B09 round 3 F09 and F10 are Owner-acceptance items and are not dispositioned here.

entries.title: OPEN_BY_OD-5: general M1 user_confirmed is self-attested
entries.statement: A bound Agent can write authority=user_explicit through the public clued_record_mutate by sending user_confirmed=true, bypassing Candidate, promotion and the Native token.
entries.consequence: Agent authority is confined only on the Information Flow path; every PASS label carries that qualifier. Such Records are Agent-authored and excluded from the default policy (E2E-12).
entries.successor: A separate Owner decision on OD-5 (tighten general M1 writes); E2E-11 expectation then flips to rejection.

entries.title: Confirmation proves a session, not a person
entries.statement: The two-step token proves a recently authenticated Native account session that performed a two-step confirmation; it cannot prove that a person rather than a script holding the session pressed the button.
entries.consequence: Contract text says human only in this sense.
entries.successor: Stronger user-presence evidence (for example WebAuthn step-up) in a later contract.

entries.title: lineage_stale and evidence_withdrawn are MSCP-only
entries.statement: The flags affect MSCP compilation only; the Record still reads CURRENT/active in Currentness, search, export and the five views until it is re-promoted, re-sourced or closed.
entries.consequence: Readers outside the Context Compiler do not see the invalidation.
entries.successor: A reviewed propagation of invalidation to other read surfaces.

entries.title: No Native-marker backfill
entries.statement: Records written before S3 (and legacy null-writer Records) read human_confirmed=false until re-confirmed.
entries.consequence: Older Native Records are excluded from default packs until re-confirmed through a Native write.
entries.successor: An Owner-authorized, Receipt-backed re-confirmation flow.

entries.title: Binding-driven denial of service under OD-5
entries.statement: A Binding can shadow State/Task through Events (a shadow needs a carrier transition) or edit/supersede the approving Decision, excluding pack items or disabling a policy until a new Native acceptance.
entries.consequence: Denial of service, not a policy change.
entries.successor: OD-5 decision; per-policy Decision write protection.

history.change: On 2026-09-29 production showed that any active global work_log Event with the decision dimension shadowed every approving Decision, so every accepted policy was refused with policy_decision_not_current (Task 9351fc10-4978-4271-9b6b-99a416d06f80). Under Owner Decision 0b183c2e-8d20-4736-8ce5-7d41ae8ce6f9, migration 20260929150000 judges the approving Decision on its own lifecycle, so an Event no longer disables a policy. A Binding can still edit or supersede the approving Decision and shadow pack items through Events, so the entry stays OPEN.

entries.title: Different confirmation strength: /v1/records marker vs two-step promotion
entries.statement: A direct Native /v1/records write gets a Native marker without a two-step token; promotion requires the two-step token.
entries.consequence: Both read human_confirmed=true in packs although their confirmation strength differs.
entries.successor: A marker strength field or a two-step option for direct Native writes.

entries.title: Contract errata carried from S1/S2
entries.statement: The implementation differs in wording from frozen v0.1: storage_ref=intake:{submission_id} (contract: candidate_id); idempotency_key lives on the submission row; knowledge_candidates has no payload column (assertion + sources); private RPC names are intake_submit_core_v1 / knowledge_propose_core_v1; the intake Evidence hash covers the canonical jsonb text of the segment.
entries.consequence: The frozen v0.1 text cannot be edited; readers must apply these errata.
entries.successor: An errata or v0.2 Decision after closeout (not in S6).

entries.title: Candidate expiry is lazy (no sweep)
entries.source: S3 D10; S5 D5; Owner deferral in S6
entries.statement: Expiry is applied only inside promotion; expired-but-pending rows still list as pending. A system sweep needs a non-additive widening of candidate_transitions.actor and a scheduler that does not exist.
entries.consequence: Pending lists can include candidates past expires_at; promotion fails closed on them.
entries.successor: Post-M0-D retention slice (design in the S6 plan section 6).

entries.title: Pack manifest retention is unbounded
entries.source: S4 D34, D27, D12; Owner deferral in S6
entries.statement: context_pack_manifests rows are never garbage-collected. A budget-refused pack leaves a manifest that revalidates VALID with token_budget_verified=false, and a context:read Binding causes Receipt-less manifest inserts.
entries.consequence: Derived, non-Canonical rows grow without bound.
entries.successor: Post-M0-D manifest GC (design in the S6 plan section 6).

entries.title: auth_time semantics verified on local GoTrue only
entries.statement: The 15-minute re-authentication rule reads amr timestamps; local GoTrue v2.195.0 tokens were exercised for real in S6, production GoTrue amr behaviour is unverified.
entries.consequence: Production behaviour must be read back before any authorized apply.
entries.successor: Production read-back under a separately authorized apply.

entries.title: Token-burn limits
entries.statement: Failures before the receipt core (malformed transport, authentication) do not burn a live confirmation token.
entries.consequence: A token survives some refused requests until its TTL.
entries.successor: None planned; disclosed.

entries.title: Delegated OAuth and Native write surfaces
entries.statement: public.clued_user_decision_supersede has been guarded by authorization_owner_v12 (direct human session; a delegated-OAuth JWT with client_id is refused) since 20260907173031. S3 (20260924190000) regressed it by redefining the entry with auth.uid(), so a delegated-OAuth JWT could supersede Decisions through PostgREST and /v1/decisions/supersede; 20260924230000_decision_supersede_v12_guard.sql (PR #322, merged to main as 982bcb3a008be00d2aaead18aae0185d816ac848; Owner Decision 9feed8c3-7720-4501-8f4f-e5604b9a3793, Receipt 817cd530-7511-456e-ab14-fcb410471365) restores the guard. Every other Native account-session RPC keeps the v12 guard, so a delegated-OAuth JWT on Native REST passes the Worker and is refused by the database.
entries.consequence: Delegated OAuth never yields a committed Native write or human_confirmed=true once 20260924230000 is applied; any environment with S3 applied but not 20260924230000 carries the regression.
entries.successor: Apply 20260924230000 wherever S3 is applied (clued-prod has S1 only per L26); a regression test pins the guard (information-flow-promotion-db.test.mjs, E2E-14 delegated block).

entries.title: Token budget enforced only on the Worker path
entries.statement: Direct PostgREST compiles are not measured (measurement not_measured); the budget is enforced by the Worker.
entries.consequence: A direct PostgREST caller can obtain an unmeasured pack.
entries.successor: Server-side token counting if the tokenizer is accepted.

entries.title: Tokenizer offline_target; production bundle and CPU unverified
entries.source: contract 6.2; S4 release impact; S6 bundle observation
entries.statement: Token counts are labelled tokenizer_status=offline_target. Bundle size and startup/first-pack CPU were observed only locally in workerd.
entries.consequence: The Cloudflare plan-limit check and a production CPU observation are a precondition of any authorized production apply (Owner decision).
entries.successor: Tokenizer acceptance; production limits check before apply.

history.change: On 2026-09-24 the production Worker was released at main 51a4fa9c on the Cloudflare Workers Free plan (Note 2d6540a4-4df8-4d2f-9717-538fabe3fd4d). A local Node measurement of js-tiktoken 1.0.21 o200k_base took 800-1556 ms CPU to construct the encoder on first use and 5-11 ms to count about 6k characters once cached, against a Free-plan limit of about 10 ms CPU per request, so the Worker measurement step of clued_context_pack is expected to exceed the limit on the Free plan. clued-prod held 0 Context Policies and 0 pack manifests, so no caller can reach the step. Owner Decision f220294c-0693-4583-a5eb-7d9eeca6d34f: upgrade to the Workers Paid plan before the first Context Policy is accepted, then observe first-pack CPU in production. No production CPU observation exists yet, so the entry stays OPEN.

entries.title: Evidence withdrawal is terminal
entries.statement: A withdrawn Evidence cannot be reinstated in MVP-0.
entries.consequence: Re-sourcing needs a new Evidence and a Receipt-backed Record write.
entries.successor: A reinstatement transition in a later contract.

entries.title: Proactive staling coverage
entries.statement: Currentness-only changes, Binding time expiry, approving-Decision edits and other candidate transitions are caught on demand at compile/revalidation, not proactively; proactive staling uses SKIP LOCKED and can skip a locked manifest.
entries.consequence: A manifest can read stale=false until revalidated; revalidation is the backstop.
entries.successor: None planned; disclosed.

entries.title: Maintenance-DML lock order
entries.statement: Maintenance writes must take currentness_user_lock first; the wrapper does, raw DML does not.
entries.consequence: Raw maintenance DML can deadlock with withdrawal fan-out.
entries.successor: Runbook rule; no code change.

entries.title: Direct M1 writes can cite withdrawn Evidence
entries.statement: A direct M1 write citing a withdrawn Evidence commits; it is flagged at write time in record_evidence_status.
entries.consequence: Such Records are excluded from compiles but remain CURRENT elsewhere (see L03).
entries.successor: None planned; disclosed.

entries.title: Withdrawal scan without index; uncapped fan-out
entries.statement: The withdrawal fan-out scans source_refs without a dedicated index and is uncapped (echoed lists are capped at 100).
entries.consequence: Large accounts may see slow withdrawals.
entries.successor: An additive index once production volumes are known.

entries.title: Transient PROJECTION_REQUIRED has no DB test
entries.statement: The PROJECTION_REQUIRED revalidation outcome is not covered by a database test.
entries.consequence: Covered only by code review.
entries.successor: A targeted test in a later slice.

entries.title: historical freshness can be authoritative; notes at any lifecycle
entries.statement: A pack under explicit historical freshness can be authoritative=true, and notes are admitted regardless of lifecycle under historical mode.
entries.consequence: Consumers must read the freshness block.
entries.successor: None planned; disclosed.

entries.title: Candidate visibility for a Binding
entries.statement: A Binding sees its own candidates and native_ui candidates in packs that allow candidate tiers.
entries.consequence: Native candidates can reach an Agent under an explicit candidate-tier policy.
entries.successor: None planned; disclosed.

entries.title: Payload-cap backstop semantics
entries.statement: The database payload cap is a backstop behind the Worker's 1 MiB body limit and reports a generic error.
entries.consequence: Oversized payloads are refused with a coarse error.
entries.successor: None planned; disclosed.

entries.title: MCP reachable in practice only with Binding tokens
entries.statement: Legacy OAuth tokens are rejected on the Information Flow MCP tools; delegated OAuth dispatches to the same Binding entries.
entries.consequence: Agents must hold a Binding.
entries.successor: None planned; disclosed.

entries.title: S6 harness residuals
entries.statement: Bindings are minted and reduced through the v12 RPCs over PostgREST with a fixture issuer row; the Worker consent API, the delegated-OAuth scopedApi/checkBinding wrapper and KV are not exercised (successor L27); issue+consume in one request is structurally impossible over HTTP (DB-level test); the kill is a SIGKILL of the workerd host group after the committed upstream response; E2E-08 restarts db/PostgREST/GoTrue/Kong and a new process; token expiry uses the real clock; the 15-minute re-authentication case stays DB-level; the harness Worker config omits global_fetch_strictly_public; the harness Worker entry is the continuity handler, not the full vinext entry; E2E-05 reduction is a PostgREST call with the owner JWT; E2E-15 (d) and (d2) need a DB fixture re-point of candidate evidence_ids and (d3) an Evidence content_hash tamper (tamperEvidenceHash, session_replication_role=replica for that one statement); the observer is read-only: where a transport read route exists (GET /v1/intake with scope/submission_id/tier, MCP clued_intake_list, the Native export route) the pass observation is the transport read and observer reads only corroborate it (E2E-07 one-row-per-key, E2E-02/E2E-15 candidate status), while the stored status of a rejected Receipt and Receipt counts (E2E-02 iii, E2E-07, E2E-15) remain observer reads because /v1/continuity/audit needs a Binding with audit:read, is keyed by context_key and returns no Receipt status; the E2E-10 Currentness/MTPE deltas and E2E-13 human_confirmed=false are internal-state observer observations, corroborated over transport by pack exclusion; E2E-10 reads the Record body through the Native export route.
entries.consequence: Evidence is local transport qualification with these disclosed substitutions.
entries.successor: None planned; disclosed.

history.previous_statement: Bindings are minted and reduced through the v12 RPCs over PostgREST with a fixture issuer row; the Worker consent API, the delegated-OAuth scopedApi/checkBinding wrapper and KV are not exercised (successor L27); issue+consume in one request is structurally impossible over HTTP (DB-level test); the kill is a SIGKILL of the workerd host group after the committed upstream response; E2E-08 restarts db/PostgREST/GoTrue/Kong and a new process; token expiry uses the real clock; the 15-minute re-authentication case stays DB-level; the harness Worker config omits global_fetch_strictly_public; the harness Worker entry is the continuity handler, not the full vinext entry; E2E-05 reduction is a PostgREST call with the owner JWT; E2E-15(b) needs a DB fixture re-point; the observer is read-only and used only for internal state with no read route; E2E-10 reads the Record body through the Native export route.

entries.title: Token session binding tolerates a JWT without session_id
entries.source: B09 round 2 F11; 20260924190000:614 and the S4/S5 token cores
entries.statement: The confirmation-token session check compares nullif(session_id) with 'is distinct from'; a JWT without a session_id claim stores NULL and the binding is then conditional on that NULL.
entries.consequence: Only an account session JWT without session_id is affected; local and hosted GoTrue password sessions carry session_id (setup.json has_session_id=true). Not changed in S6.
entries.successor: Additive hotfix migration (like PR #322) requiring a non-null session_id at token issue in S3/S4/S5.
entries.reason_not_fixed_in_s6: The fix redefines large SECURITY DEFINER token functions from three slices; S6 adds no migration and schema fixes go through a separate reviewed hotfix PR, as for PR #322.

resolution.commit_note: Introduced in 0d4e0db9; the consume check was revised (same helper normalizes issue and consume) in the follow-up review-minors commit on the same branch, which records this migration_sha256.
resolution.fix: The S3, S4 and S5 confirmation-issue cores reject a JWT without a non-empty string session_id claim with confirmation_token_session_id_required (no token row is written); every consume requires a non-null token session_id equal to the JWT's (both normalized by clued_private.native_session_id_v1), otherwise confirmation_token_binding_mismatch. A NULL-session token issued before the migration can no longer be consumed.

entries.title: Native token lookup is not filtered by action before burn
entries.statement: The native_confirmation_tokens lookup in the consume path does not filter by action before burning, so a user's own token issued for one action can be burned by presenting it to another action's RPC.
entries.consequence: Same-user self denial of service only; a burned token is never accepted for the other action.
entries.successor: Additive hotfix migration adding the action filter before burn.
entries.reason_not_fixed_in_s6: Same as L29: a separate reviewed schema hotfix, not an S6 migration.

resolution.commit_note: Introduced in 0d4e0db9; the consume check was revised (same helper normalizes issue and consume) in the follow-up review-minors commit on the same branch, which records this migration_sha256.
resolution.fix: The locking token lookups in clued_private.context_policy_accept_core_v1 and clued_private.evidence_withdraw_core_v1 filter by action (context_policy_accept, evidence_withdraw), matching their pre-shape-check lookups; a token for one action reads confirmation_token_invalid at the other action's RPC and is not burned. The subject key is deliberately not added: a same-action token presented for another subject is still burned as confirmation_token_binding_mismatch, the single-use rule S3 applies to a token for another candidate (E2E-15).
resolution.tests: apps/clued-cloud/tests/information-flow-token-hardening-db.test.mjs (npm run test:information-flow:hardening; reproduces the defect on the chain before the migration, asserts the fix after it); also covers cross-user presentation and anchor drift (no helper, no partial patch)

entries.title: Go CLI children and Miniflare's workerd child are not under the Node isolation guard
entries.source: B09 round 2 F08; B09 round 3 F05
entries.statement: The Supabase CLI (a Go binary) and Docker CLI calls made by the harness cannot load the Node guard; they run with an allowlisted environment without proxy variables or cloud credentials, and only against the local stack. Wrangler dry-run runs under the guard. Each Worker host's Miniflare also starts a native workerd child, which is not a Node process and cannot load the guard; its Worker fetch() egress is bounded by the Miniflare outboundService ledger (only the loopback Supabase gateway is forwarded, anything else is answered 599 and recorded; isolation.json worker_egress), and isolation.json harness_egress.unguarded_children lists it.
entries.consequence: Their egress is bounded by the scrubbed environment (CLIs) or by outboundService (workerd fetch), not by an in-process ledger.
entries.successor: None planned; disclosed.

history.previous_title: Go CLI children of the harness are not under the Node isolation guard

entries.title: Normalized digests are a reproducibility aid, not a byte seal
entries.source: B09 round 2 F10; B09 round 3 F08
entries.statement: The per-scenario normalized digest covers channel, method, target template, HTTP status, extracted values, assertion ids/expected values/pass and the result, with ids, digests, timestamps, PIDs and durations replaced and arrays sorted. It drops step ledgers, assertion observed values and notes.
entries.consequence: Byte integrity of each evidence file comes from SHA256SUMS; equal normalized digests at the same code tree show that two runs produced the same pattern of steps, statuses, extracted values and assertion pass/fail results, not that every observed value was identical (assertion observed values are dropped).
entries.successor: None planned; documented in the harness README.

history.previous_consequence: Byte integrity of each evidence file comes from SHA256SUMS; the normalized digest shows that two runs at the same code tree made the same observations.
